newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwanda tribunal postpones hearing for defence.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal postpones hearing for defence.

text.p: The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda postponed on Wednesday the trial of a former mayor accused of genocide to allow the defence time to prepare its case.

The trial of Jean-Paul Akayesu, former mayor of Taba commune in central Rwanda, was delayed until September 29 at a closed-door session after the prosecution's 22nd and last witness finished giving evidence.

Akayesu's defence was hampered because witnesses were reluctant to testify fearing reprisals from the government that came to power after the genocide, said defence counsel Patrice Monthe of Cameroon.
Akayesu has pleaded not guilty to charges of genocide and crimes against humanity. He faces life imprisonment if convicted, the tribunal's highest penalty.
The U.N. Rwanda tribunal has been plagued by problems in attempting to bring to justice the leaders of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.
So far 21 people have been indicted by the Rwanda tribunal, which has a total of 12 suspects in detention in Arusha, north Tanzania.
